notes.note:
[Firefox for Android][1] now includes stronger [protection against fingerprinting][2] in Standard Enhanced Tracking Protection, making it harder for websites to track people across sites by limiting the amount of information revealed about their device and browser. ([Learn more][3])


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix
  [2]: https://support.mozilla.org/kb/firefox-protection-against-fingerprinting
  [3]: https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/fingerprinting-protections/
The keyboard shortcut for copying the current tab's URL now removes tracking parameters from the copied link.

Firefox now supports [streaming uploads][1] with the [Fetch API][2], allowing web applications to send request bodies incrementally using a `ReadableStream` without buffering the entire body first.


  [1]: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/fetch-streaming-requests
  [2]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API/Using_Fetch

Firefox now supports the [`headingoffset`][1] and [`headingreset`][2] attributes, which let authors shift the level of headings inside an element, or reset that shift, without changing the heading elements themselves.

  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/headingoffset
  [2]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/headingreset

Firefox now supports the [Regular Expression Buffer Boundaries proposal][1], adding `\A`, `\z`, and `\Z` character escapes to Unicode-mode regular expressions.


  [1]: https://github.com/tc39/proposal-regexp-buffer-boundaries

Firefox now accepts [declarative push messages][1]. Push messages sent in the declarative format are shown directly shown as notifications without involving a service worker, and push subscriptions can now be managed through `window.pushManager`.


  [1]: https://w3c.github.io/push-api/#declarative-push-message

Firefox now fires `mousedown`, `mouseup`, and `auxclick` events for the back and forward mouse buttons (X1 and X2), with [`button`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/MouseEvent/button) set to `3` and `4` respectively. Calling `preventDefault()` on the `mouseup` or `auxclick` event prevents the default action of the button, which is usually to navigate back or forward.
Fixed address bar results covering the address bar in macOS full screen when the menu bar was revealed.
Fixed context menu items sometimes appearing blank, without their labels, after Firefox was updated.

On [Firefox for Android][1], long-pressing some images now shows the image description as expected.


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix

Fixed [Firefox for Android][1] not switching between light and dark theme to match the device if the setting changed while Firefox was still open.


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix
Fixed windows not being restored to their saved positions on GNOME 51 and later when Firefox is set to restore the previous session.
Fixed the Copy and Download buttons in the Screenshots overlay not responding to touchscreen taps.
Fixed the page jumping out of view while typing on some sites, such as the New York Times crossword.
Fixed some HDR videos appearing washed out in full screen on Windows when using a non-HDR display.

system_requirements:
## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio

Firefox Beta gets updated 3 times a week and as a consequence, the release notes for the Beta channel are updated continuously to reflect features that have reached sufficient maturity to benefit from community feedback and bug reports.
Warning: Features listed here may or may not make a final release of Firefox

In addition to these release notes, you can follow ongoing development via the [Firefox Trains][1] website or our [@FirefoxBeta][2] Bluesky account. [1]: https://whattrainisitnow.com/beta/ [2]: https://bsky.app/profile/firefoxbeta.bsky.social
